title: Global scalar factors for boundary residuals
reviewed_arguments: H0 retains complete residual kernels, compact boundary, all side-flat seminorms and the original Banach norm; common and varying inputs have their actual quantifiers.
C0 proves the global collar from finite cutoffs and the actual smooth flow; the density-normalizing unitary is computed with its half powers.

C1 fixes all support buffers and the normal bump before the family-dependent envelope. Every cross-chart and cross-component corner remains; only a true original smooth flat-input remainder receives the coarse Banach bound.
J0 proves the atlas isometry with exact density adjoints. Product torus completeness is obtained by successive circle projections, including the finite zero-dimensional case.
J1 uses integration by parts in the full tangential kernel and a joint discrete tail. J2 extends a uniformly square-summable column series, without declaring the inverse diagonal bounded.

P0 proves the contraction, all binomial series coefficients, positivity, norm Cauchy product and squared identity. P1 proves the scalar tangential square root has a joint smooth kernel; it does not take the square root of a full b-residual.
P2 proves density of the range, the elementary closed-subspace projection fact and the actual auxiliary isometry. No extra vector-valued test is asserted.

N0 retains two actual normal reciprocal derivatives with an integrable frequency weight. N1 twice integrates the full operator-valued Fourier kernel and proves both Schur integrals by the same difference majorant.
N2 gives exact Fourier cancellation, the correct full density and ratio kernel, compact input/output projections and side flatness. N3 uses only the actual smooth graph completion.
All three solutions and the figure were checked. All13 final reader captures were actually viewed;306 formulas and17 tagged displays parse, and every mobile formula/figure extent is accessible.
The finite-order global scalar gluing and full general observation theorem are expressly not proved by this residual lemma.
